slides.0.title: Gigondas, Vacqueyras and the other southern crus
slides.0.subtitle: Rules and styles of the southern crus
slides.1.title: Gigondas and Vacqueyras
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Gigondas: 1971
slides.1.highlights.0.content: Decree of 6 January 1971; in the commune of Gigondas (Vaucluse) beneath the Dentelles de Montmirail. Red, rosé and — from the 2023 vintage — white. About 1,184 ha in 2025
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Gigondas varieties
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Red and rosé: Grenache at least 50%; Cinsault, Mourvèdre and Syrah together at least 15%. The older Drive note ("Syrah + Mourvèdre at least 15%") omits Cinsault — INAO governs. White (approved by INAO in September 2022): Clairette at least 70%
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Vacqueyras: 1990
slides.1.highlights.2.content: Recognised in 1990 (the INAO text gives 9 and 15 August in two places, the year agrees); the communes of Sarrians and Vacqueyras; red, rosé and white. About 1,421 ha in 2025 (white about 7%)
slides.1.highlights.3.title: Vacqueyras rules
slides.1.highlights.3.content: Red: Grenache at least 50% and Syrah + Mourvèdre at least 20%; both appellations have a 36 hl/ha yield (ceiling 40); red minimum natural alcohol 12.5%
slides.1.content: Both are built on at least 50% Grenache, with yields of 36 hl/ha.
slides.2.title: Vinsobres, Beaumes-de-Venise and Cairanne
slides.2.highlights.0.title: Vinsobres: 2006
slides.2.highlights.0.content: February 2006 decree (the INAO text gives 15th and 17th); the only southern cru in the Drôme. Red: Grenache at least 50%, Syrah + Mourvèdre at least 25%; yield 38 hl/ha; about 559 ha in 2025. Whites appear in the current draft
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Beaumes-de-Venise: 2005
slides.2.highlights.1.content: The dry red became a cru in 2005 (decree of 25 October); four communes: Beaumes-de-Venise, Lafare, La Roque-Alric and Suzette. Grenache at least 50%, Syrah at least 20% (Syrah + Mourvèdre at least 25%); yield 38 hl/ha; about 738 ha in 2025. The Muscat VDN is a separate AOC (lesson 7)
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Cairanne: 2016
slides.2.highlights.2.content: Applied for in 2008 after eight years of negotiation, approved in February 2016 and retroactive to the 2015 harvest (iDealwine); red and white. About 886 ha in 2025. It could add its name to Côtes du Rhône from 1953 and to Villages from 1967
slides.2.highlights.3.title: Cairanne proportions: not tested
slides.2.highlights.3.content: The 2026 draft strikes the Grenache floor from 50% to 40% and the white-grape cap from 5% to 15% (Syrah + Mourvèdre at least 20% in red). The draft is still in procedure, so no conclusion is given and it is not tested
slides.2.content: The three promotions came in 2005, 2006 and 2016.
slides.3.title: Rasteau and Laudun
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Rasteau: VDN and dry red
slides.3.highlights.0.content: First recognised by decree of 5 January 1944 as a vin doux naturel (VDN) AOC; the dry red became a cru in 2010 and must come from the commune of Rasteau. Dry red: Grenache at least 50%, 38 hl/ha, minimum natural alcohol 12.5%
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Rasteau VDN
slides.3.highlights.1.content: Styles: blanc, ambré, grenat, rosé and tuilé, with rancio allowed on ambré and tuilé; Grenache at least 75% for grenat and tuilé. Fortified with neutral spirit of at least 96% vol., 5–10% of the must volume; must sugar at least 252 g/L; 30 hl of must/ha
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Residual-sugar numbers in old notes
slides.3.highlights.2.content: Drive notes give residual sugar minima of 45 g/L (Rasteau VDN) and 100 g/L (Muscat de Beaumes-de-Venise); the INAO text read here states only 252 g/L natural must sugar, so the residual figures could not be confirmed and are not tested
slides.3.highlights.3.title: Laudun: 2024
slides.3.highlights.3.content: On 11 September 2024 the INAO national committee approved Côtes du Rhône Villages Laudun as the AOP "Laudun"; three Gard communes: Laudun-l'Ardoise, Saint-Victor-la-Coste and Tresques. Red: Grenache at least 50% and Syrah at least 25%; the draft specification lists red and white. Area differs by source (about 580 ha in the draft, 512 ha in 2025) and is not tested
slides.3.content: Rasteau is one name for two wines: the dry red is a cru, the VDN an earlier AOC.
slides.4.title: Lirac and Tavel: two right-bank crus
slides.4.highlights.0.title: Lirac
slides.4.highlights.0.content: Decree of 14 October 1947; four Gard communes: Lirac, Roquemaure, Saint-Geniès-de-Comolas and Saint-Laurent-des-Arbres. Red, rosé and white; red and rosé need at least 40% Grenache and 25% Syrah + Mourvèdre; yield 41 hl/ha (ceiling 43). About 848 ha in 2025
slides.4.highlights.1.title: Tavel: rosé only
slides.4.highlights.1.content: Decree of 15 May 1936; the specification allows still rosé only; Tavel plus a few parcels in Roquemaure. Yield 46 hl/ha (ceiling 50); minimum natural alcohol 11.5%; about 781 ha in 2025
slides.4.highlights.2.title: Tavel variety rules
slides.4.highlights.2.content: Grenache (noir, blanc and gris together) must exceed 30% and stay under 60%, and Grenache noir must be in every blend; white grapes such as Clairette and Bourboulenc are among the main varieties, each at most 60%
slides.4.highlights.3.title: What they share
slides.4.highlights.3.content: Both lie on the right bank in the Gard, facing Châteauneuf-du-Pape across the river; Tavel specialises in rosé while Lirac makes red, rosé and white (red about 83% in 2025)
slides.4.content: Tavel (1936) and Lirac (1947) were recognised long before most southern crus.
slides.5.componentProps.slide.title: 🧠 Knowledge Check
In which year was the Gigondas decree issued?
6 January 1971 (INAO and the Drive notes agree). 1990 is Vacqueyras.
Which of these crus was promoted most recently?
Laudun, approved by the INAO national committee on 11 September 2024, is the 18th cru.
In Rasteau VDN, how much neutral spirit is added, as a share of the must volume?
5% to 10% (neutral spirit of at least 96% vol.), with must sugar at least 252 g/L.
Which statement about Tavel is correct?
A. Rosé only, and Grenache noir must be in every blend
B. Red, rosé and white all allowed
C. Located on the left bank
Tavel makes only still rosé, lies on the right bank in the Gard, and Grenache noir must be in every blend.
